exclusions.A: I am too old to cry before everybody, but I didn't wish any more dinner, and as soon as possible I went up to my room and had a good cry.
exclusions.B: "Well, if he would only soften it a little," I couldn't help saying.
exclusions.D: If I can't, I can't; it does seem hard though never to do as the others do.
exclusions.E: A blunt no is a great deal harder to bear.

PD2-P2-5.note: The eighth paragraph is the narrator wishing her father would 'soften it a little' and saying 'a blunt no is a great deal harder to bear', which is a criticism of how he refuses; it is not amusement, tenderness, scorn of his worry, or appreciation of his frankness.
